en.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable.
Statement II : As bond order increases, the bond length increases.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
en.sol: Statement I is false: bond order 0 means no net bonding, so such a molecule does not exist (e.g. He2). Statement II is false: higher bond order means a shorter bond. Both false.
en.hint: Bond order ↑ → bond length ↓, stability ↑.

कथन II : आबंध कोटि बढ़ने पर आबंध लंबाई बढ़ती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

en.q:
Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned:
A. H2O > NH3 > CHCl3 - dipole moment
B. XeF4 > XeO3 > XeF2 - number of lone pairs on central atom
C. O − H > C − H > N − O - bond length
D. N2 > O2 > H2 - bond enthalpy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
en.sol:
• A ✓ dipole moments: H2O 1.85 D > NH3 1.47 D > CHCl3 ≈ 1.0 D.
  • B ✗ lone pairs on Xe: XeF4 2, XeO3 1, XeF2 3.
  • C ✗ O–H (96 pm) is shorter than C–H (109 pm).
  • D ✓ bond enthalpies: N2 946 > O2 498 > H2 436 kJ mol−1.

Answer: A, D only.
en.hint: Triple bond in N<sub>2</sub>; XeF<sub>2</sub> has three lone pairs.

en.q:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Molecule): (A) ethane (B) Ethene (C) carbon molecule, C2 (D) ethyne
List II (Number and types of bond/s between two carbon atoms): (I) one σ-bond and two π-bonds (II) two π-bonds (III) one σ-bond (IV) one σ-bond and one π-bond
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
en.sol:
Ethane C–C: one σ (III). Ethene C=C: one σ + one π (IV). C2 (MO theory): two π bonds, no σ (II). Ethyne C≡C: one σ + two π (I).

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
en.hint: C<sub>2</sub> is NCERT's example of a molecule with only π bonds.

en.q:
[Lewis structure of O3 with the central oxygen numbered 1 and the end oxygens numbered 2 and 3, as drawn in the paper]
The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 respectively are :
en.sol:
Formal charge = V − L − ½B (NCERT §4.1.4). In the drawn structure O2 is double-bonded (6 − 4 − 2 = 0), central O1 has one lone pair and three bonds (6 − 2 − 3 = +1), O3 is single-bonded with three lone pairs (6 − 6 − 1 = −1).

Answer: 0, +1, −1.
en.hint: FC = valence electrons − non-bonding electrons − ½ bonding electrons.

en.q: The variation of the boiling points of the hydrogen halides is in the order HF > HI > HBr > HCl. What explains the higher boiling point of hydrogen fluoride ?
o: The electronegativity of fluorine is much higher than for other elements in the group.
There is strong hydrogen bonding between HF molecules.
The bond energy of HF molecules is greater than in other hydrogen halides.
The effect of nuclear shielding is much reduced in fluorine which polarises the HF molecule.
en.sol: F is small and highly electronegative, so HF molecules are linked by strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds; extra energy is needed to separate them, giving HF the highest boiling point. Among HCl, HBr, HI the boiling point rises with molar mass (van der Waals forces).
en.hint: The anomaly is the same as for H<sub>2</sub>O and NH<sub>3</sub>.
